fight: How hard his armies fight (multiplies army quality)
bleed: How many men his armies lose in battle (multiplier)
land: What a conquered province is worth to him (multiplier)
distrust: What neighbours' distrust costs him when he weighs a war (multiplier)
revenge: What winning back a lost province is worth to him (multiplier)
threat: How large every threat looks to him (multiplier)
waste: Share of all gold wasted on the court each season
buildTime: Seasons a factory takes to build
borrow: Gold he will borrow to build a factory
horizon: Years he plans ahead, whatever his patience
reformWait: Seasons before he can pass reforms again
hold: Chance a battle in or against his land changes nothing
allies: What an alliance is worth to him (multiplier)
broker: Chance a season that he brokers peace in a neighbour's war
brokerAfter: Seasons a war must have lasted before he steps in
brokerScore: He steps in only while neither side is winning by more than this
fee: Share of each side's gold he is paid for a peace
feeCap: Most gold he takes from each side for a peace
friendship: Relations he starts with his favourite great power
join: Chance he joins a war on his favourite's side
ownPeople: What provinces of his own people pay (multiplier)
misjudge: How far his judgment swings each season, either way
changeEvery: On average, seasons between his changes of quirk
charm: Relations he gains with every neighbour when crowned
ofAge: Seasons until he comes of age (fewest, most)
unrest: Unrest he adds everywhere until he wins a war
keepGold: Share of the gold left after his coup
calm: Unrest taken away (at once for a usurper, every season for a saint)
legitimacy: Yearly gold a victory is worth to him by ending the unrest of his reign, as a share of gold a year
distrusted: Relations he loses with every neighbour when crowned
infamy: Distrust he starts his reign with
works: Seasons until his landmark is finished
coup: Chance a season that the nobles depose him
garrison: Strength of his garrisons against uprisings (multiplier)
integrate: How fast his conquests become integrated (multiplier)
settle: Share of the time a conquest takes to become integrated that he counts when he weighs a war
rise: Unrest added at his death to the provinces it touches
integration: How far integrated his conquests are left at his death, at most
debtYears: Years of gold a year that turn into debt at his death
levy: Raises a great army when crowned (see rules: levy)
isolates: No ally comes to his enemy's aid and no great power steps in
keepsAll: Every victory keeps all the occupied land he can reach
converts: Every people he conquers counts as his own at once
crisis: His death brings civil war ("bastard": his bastard son claims the throne)
hated: Three times as likely to be assassinated (see rules: reign)
